price_notes: Dry or extensive parcels 8,000 to 20,000 EUR/ha and irrigated Alqueva-zone land 25,000 to 45,000 EUR/ha come from market reports and listings (Idealista, CBRE, Savills) that were not opened (not verified). The dossier's 'Portugal national arable mean 11,827 EUR/ha (Eurostat 2024)' is not what the cited release shows: Eurostat's 2024 release lists Portugal arable land at 76,556 EUR/ha, which is not comparable with dry extensive parcels, so the 11,827 figure is dropped.
appreciation_notes: Dossier states the trajectory is firmly upward as wine, olive, almond and regen-investment demand intensifies (not verified).
source: Idealista Alentejo listings, CBRE Property Handbook 2024 and Savills Global Farmland September 2024 (none opened); Eurostat agricultural land prices 2024 release (opened, national figure only)
gaps: No regional official price series was opened; the range rests on market reports.

price_notes: Galicia average 19,335 EUR/ha in 2024 (MAPA definitive 2024, Cuadro 1; +4.2% on 2023; all uses, so it includes intensive and vineyard land); Spain 10,248 EUR/ha (+2.8%). The dossier's use-class ranges (dry pasture 3,000 to 8,000; productive prado or labradío 8,000 to 18,000; Ribeira Sacra and Rías Baixas vineyard land 40,000 to 80,000 and over, from Vinetur) were not verified and are not used for the range.
source: MAPA, Precios medios anuales de las tierras de uso agrario 2024 (definitive), Cuadro 1
gaps: The regional mean covers all land uses of the autonomous community; parcel prices for rough pasture or abandoned holdings were not found in an opened source.

price_notes: Romania national averages 2024 (Eurostat apri_lprc): permanent grassland 6,257 EUR/ha and arable land 8,700 EUR/ha; INSSE gives a national average of 8,656 EUR/ha. National figures, not Transylvania-specific. The dossier's class ranges (pasture or marginal 4,000 to 7,000; arable 7,000 to 10,000; high-quality irrigated Mureș basin 12,000 to 18,000) come from consultancy commentary that was not opened (not verified).
appreciation_notes: Eurostat: arable 8,414 EUR/ha (2023) to 8,700 (2024), +3.4%; grassland 6,074 to 6,257, +3.0%. The dossier's 25 to 40 percent over a decade was not verified.
source: Eurostat apri_lprc (national, 2024); INSSE, Agricultural land prices in Romania and EU Member States in 2024
gaps: Smaller-parcel sales in remote Carpathian villages often transact below national averages and are not captured; no county series was opened.

price_notes: CSO table ARA02 (Agricultural Land Prices 2024, median price per acre, all land): West region (Galway, Mayo, Roscommon) 7,027 EUR/acre (about 17,360 EUR/ha); South-West (Cork and Kerry) 10,914 EUR/acre (about 26,970 EUR/ha); Ireland 9,988 EUR/acre (about 24,680 EUR/ha). The dossier's 'Cork region 17,875 EUR/acre' does not appear in the CSO table and is dropped. Marginal Connemara mountain and bog land often below 5,000 EUR/acre is a dossier statement (not verified). Per-acre to per-ha via /0.4047.
appreciation_notes: National YoY change 2023 to 2024 +10.3% per CSO Ireland.
source: CSO Ireland, Agricultural Land Prices 2024 (table ARA02, regional breakdown)
gaps: Connemara-specific medians are not broken out in the CSO release; the range spans the West and South-West region medians.

price_notes: Pembrokeshire bare land 8,000 to 11,000 GBP/acre (about 19,770 to 27,180 GBP/ha) for mixed or grass land and prime parcels above 20,000 GBP/acre come from a Wales and England aggregate attributed to the Knight Frank Farmland Index (9,152 GBP/acre); the index page was not opened and no Pembrokeshire-only figure was found (not verified). Per-acre to per-ha via /0.4047.
appreciation_notes: Marginal rise from 9,152 to 9,164 GBP/acre between Q4 2024 and early 2025 in the Wales and England aggregate attributed to Knight Frank (not verified).
source: Knight Frank Farmland Index Q4 2024 (research page only; the index was not opened); Farmers Weekly, Farmland in your area, Wales 2024
gaps: No Pembrokeshire-only figure and no opened index page; the figures are an aggregate for Wales and England.

price_notes: Lozère 5,480 EUR/ha (+8.1% YoY); Ardèche about 5,500 to 7,000 (2023); Aude 6,360; Hérault 7,900; Gard 13,240 (wine-zone weighted); Occitanie free-land average 7,280 EUR/ha. These are attributed to the Safer price scale and Agreste; the Safer series page renders its figures by script and the values were not read (not verified).
appreciation_notes: Dossier: Lozère +8.1% in 2024 and very strong growth in the Cévennes and Causses (not verified).
source: Safer, Le prix des terres (Occitanie series); Agreste
gaps: Departmental figures were not read from the Safer page; the Safer scale (barème) PDF was not opened.

price_notes: No verified South Tirol land price. The earlier range of 47,100 to 1,100,000 EUR/ha mixed land classes and is withdrawn: its low end, 'North-East Italy agricultural land average 47,100 EUR/ha (Eurostat 2024)', is not in the Eurostat apri_lprc dataset (no Italian value for 2023 or 2024; Eurostat's release says Italy's latest figures are from earlier years), and its high end is DOC vineyard land (300,000 to 500,000 EUR/ha in Val Venosta and Isarco; 600,000 to 1,100,000 around Lake Caldaro, from wine-press summaries, not verified), a land class that a settlement would not buy. Italy national mean about 22,400 EUR/ha (CREA, +1%) is a dossier figure and was not verified.
appreciation_notes: Supply of land is constrained by the closed-farm (maso chiuso) regime (see the legal layer); no price trend was verified.
source: Eurostat apri_lprc (opened: no value for Italy 2023 to 2024); CREA 2024 and wine-press summaries (not opened)
gaps: No official South Tirol or Alto Adige price series was opened. Mountain pasture (Almweide) values are distorted by the closed-farm regime and rarely transact on the open market.

price_notes: Principado de Asturias regional mean 10,956 EUR/ha (MAPA 2024 definitive, Cuadro 1; +3.3% on 2023: 10,605; 2022: 10,232); Spain national average 10,248 EUR/ha (+2.8%). Asturias is about 7% above the national mean, not below it. The dossier's use-class ranges (permanent pasture 5,000 to 10,000; arable 10,000 to 15,000; mountain marginal land 1,500 to 4,000 EUR/ha) were not checked against the MAPA class tables (not verified) and are not used for the range.
source: MAPA, Precios medios anuales de las tierras de uso agrario 2024 (definitive), Cuadro 1
gaps: The regional mean covers all uses; variance by valley and use class is wide and the class tables were not read.

price_notes: Average purchase price for Ackerland 22,022 EUR/ha and rental 429 EUR/ha are attributed to an agrarheute analysis of state statistics; the 22,022 figure appears only in a map graphic of that article and was not read (not verified). Bodenrichtwert 2.00 EUR/m2 (20,000 EUR/ha) from the Gutachterausschuss was not opened (not verified). The Magdeburger Börde black-earth soils are priced higher (not verified).
appreciation_notes: Conflicting: the dossier reports the Bodenrichtwert stable in 2024 (not verified), while the agrarheute article lists Saxony-Anhalt among the Länder where Destatis Ackerland purchase prices fell in 2024 (about 4%), and German arable prices fell for the first time in 2025 according to the same outlet.
source: agrarheute, Bodenpreise: So viel kostete ein Hektar Ackerland 2024 (opened; the figure sits in a graphic); Gutachterausschuss Sachsen-Anhalt (not opened)
gaps: The EUR 22,022/ha value could not be read from the article text; no state statistical-office table was opened.

price_notes: Eurostat apri_lprc national averages for Estonia: permanent grassland 5,274 EUR/ha (2024; 4,617 in 2023) and arable land 7,033 EUR/ha (2024; 6,347 in 2023). Saaremaa and Setomaa transact below the national average (no official regional series found). The dossier's pasture 2,000 to 4,000 and arable 3,500 to 5,500 EUR/ha (labelled 2023, interpolated from industry reporting) sit below Eurostat's official averages and are dropped.
appreciation_notes: Eurostat: arable +10.8% (6,347 to 7,033 EUR/ha) and permanent grassland +14.2% (4,617 to 5,274) from 2023 to 2024.
source: Eurostat apri_lprc, Estonia, 2023 and 2024
gaps: National averages; no regional series for the footprint was opened.

price_notes: Scottish Land Commission Rural Land Market Data Report 2025, Highlands and Islands region (Argyll, Bute, Caithness, Inverness, Nairn, Orkney and Zetland, Ross and Cromarty, Sutherland; wider than the footprint). Low: estate sales 2020-2024, GBP 115,865,548 over 57,437 ha = about GBP 2,017/ha (derived; 47 sales, mean sale GBP 2,465,224). High: farmland 2024 mean GBP 9,497/ha (17 sales, 1,590 ha); 2020-2024 farmland mean GBP 7,578/ha over 98 sales. The report says croft tenancies and farmland bought for housing are excluded where possible; croft and housing-plot prices were not found in any official series.
appreciation_notes: Highlands and Islands farmland mean per ha: GBP 5,140 (2020), 6,713 (2021), 7,540 (2022), 8,051 (2023), 9,497 (2024) on 11 to 29 sales a year; in the same report national forestry values fell from GBP 15,327/ha in 2023 to 10,054 in 2024 and estate sales fell to the lowest count in five years, so the thin marginal-land market moves in both directions.
source: Scottish Land Commission, Rural Land Market Data Report 2025 (Registers of Scotland sales data 2020-2024)
gaps: A land price is not the entry cost: house and plot prices, croft prices (asking prices only on listing sites, not opened), Savills and Knight Frank Scottish indices (Savills returned 429) and Registers of Scotland statistics (403) were not opened. The England-only Knight Frank series is deliberately not used. Land and Buildings Transaction Tax on non-residential land: 0% to GBP 150,000, 1% to 250,000, 5% above (Revenue Scotland).

price_notes: Forest-only unbuilt properties over 2 ha in sparsely populated areas, median price per hectare 2025 by municipality (National Land Survey purchase price register, representative sales): lowest Ristijärvi 2,869, highest Kitee 6,279; 433 sales across the 18 municipalities. Sale-weighted mean of municipal medians 4,698. Counties: North Karelia median 5,191 (321 sales), Kainuu 2,969 (180 sales, includes municipalities outside the footprint). Cultivated land only, unbuilt: North Karelia median 4,850 (25 sales), Kainuu 2,312 (8 sales); Luke NUTS2 Northern and Eastern Finland agricultural land 6,013 EUR/ha in 2025. Unbuilt shore holiday plots in sparsely populated areas, median per m2 2025: North Karelia 2.62 (4 sales), Kainuu 2.00 (5 sales); sample sizes are very small.
appreciation_notes: Sale-weighted mean of footprint municipal forest medians 4,330 (2023), 4,266 (2024), 4,698 (2025); county forest medians 2021 to 2025: North Karelia 3,919 to 5,191 (+32%), Kainuu 2,136 to 2,969 (+39%), whole country 3,168 to 4,405 (+39%). Agricultural land (Luke NUTS2) fell from 6,488 (2022) to 5,482 (2024) before 6,013 in 2025.
source: National Land Survey of Finland, purchase price statistics (kauppahintarekisteri), tables 4.1, 4.3, 5.3; Luke land purchase prices
gaps: Whole-property prices with buildings are not covered (forest-only unbuilt and cultivated-only unbuilt parcels, 95% forest land, 600-15,000 EUR parcel filter). Municipal medians rest on 5 to 54 sales each. Kainuu county figures include Hyrynsalmi, Suomussalmi and Puolanka. Shore plot prices from 4 to 5 sales a year.

price_notes: Free, unbuilt farmland and meadow, petites régions agricoles 'Plateau de Millevaches': Creuse 2,040 EUR/ha, Corrèze (Artense, Plateau de Millevaches) 3,070, Haute-Vienne 3,730. Departmental means 2,890 (Creuse), 3,880 (Corrèze, range 930 to 8,000), 3,550 (Haute-Vienne). Rented land 2,140 to 2,990. Woodland: Massif Central forest region 2,850 EUR/ha. Statistical averages, not appraisals.
appreciation_notes: 2025 versus 2024: Creuse departmental price stable, Haute-Vienne +1%, Corrèze +2% (Artense plateau +9%, small market); Safer reports prices stabilising in every Nouvelle-Aquitaine département.
source: Safer / Le prix des terres 2025 (series with the Ministry of Agriculture and INSEE)
gaps: Averages blend land of very uneven quality; no parcel-level or woodland departmental price opened (the 4,950 EUR/ha shown on departmental forest pages is the France-wide figure); built property excluded.

price_notes: Teruel PROVINCE 2024 definitive (February 2026 release) MAPA class means: pastizal 1,508 EUR/ha (266,767 ha weight); tierra arable secano 2,692 (342,033 ha); frutos secos secano 3,035; olivar secano 2,920; arable regadio 7,592; olivar regadio 8,090; frutos secos regadio 7,300; frutal carnoso regadio 12,682. Area-weighted mean 2,523 EUR/ha (derived here from MAPA tables 20 and 21, base-2020 weights; MAPA does not print it). Aragon mean 5,175 EUR/ha; Spain 10,248 EUR/ha. Province-level, includes the Ebro-side lowland comarcas that are outside the footprint; no comarca-level series opened. Rural houses are not priced here.
appreciation_notes: Aragon mean 4,369 EUR/ha (2020) to 5,175 (2024): +18.5% (index 118.5) against Spain +13.8% (index 113.8); Aragon 2023-24 +3.4%. No Teruel-only series in the table opened.
source: MAPA, Precios medios anuales de las tierras de uso agrario 2024 (definitive), tables 1, 20, 21
gaps: Comarca agraria prices were not opened and the weighted mean is derived. Much of the footprint's land is held by villagers, municipalities and the Comunidad, and entry is by invitation rather than by purchase. The stored range spans several land classes (the high end is 8 times the low end), so the band is a rough bucket of its middle.

price_notes: Agenzia delle Entrate Valori Agricoli Medi 2025, Cuneo (commission of 13 Jan 2025), EUR/ha. Regione agraria 2 (high Maira and Grana): pascolo 1,394, bosco d'alto fusto 2,546, prato 4,325, seminativo 5,004, prato irriguo 9,084. Regione agraria 3 (mid Maira, incl. Dronero): prato 8,959, seminativo 8,959, prato irriguo 18,477. Low is pasture, high is irrigated meadow; irrigated arable, orchard and vegetable land (21,565 to 30,479) excluded. These are statutory compensation values, not asking prices.
appreciation_notes: Statutory VAM, regione agraria 2 prato: 3,922 (2021), 4,159 (2023), 4,325 (2024 and 2025); pascolo 1,263 to 1,394. About +10 percent over four years and unchanged 2024 to 2025; this tracks a tariff review, not market transactions.
source: Agenzia delle Entrate, Valori Agricoli Medi, Provincia di Cuneo 2025 (and 2024, 2023, 2021)
gaps: No market-transaction prices (CREA land-value database not opened); no borgata or house prices (OMI quotations not retrieved); fragmented small parcels and heirs' shares are not reflected in tariffs. The stored range spans several land classes (the high end is 13 times the low end), so the band is a rough bucket of its middle.

price_notes: USDA NASS Land Values 2024 Summary, Oregon: farm real estate 3,720 USD/acre (about 9,190 USD/ha); cropland 4,350 (irrigated cropland 7,650 in the regional table); pasture 1,050. The dossier's 'Oregon farm real estate average 2,380 USD/acre' matches no year of the table and is dropped. The range kept here, unimproved timber and foothills 1,500 to 4,000 USD/acre (3,700 to 9,880 USD/ha) and Willamette Valley irrigated cropland 8,000 to 16,000 USD/acre (19,760 to 39,530 USD/ha), is a dossier estimate attributed to Farmer Mac and is not in the NASS table (not verified); the statewide NASS figures include eastern Oregon. 'Western Oregon costs 3 to 5x the Alentejo baseline' is a dossier statement (not verified). Per-acre to per-ha via /0.4047.
appreciation_notes: NASS Oregon farm real estate: 2,630 (2020), 2,950, 3,280, 3,500, 3,720 USD/acre (2024; +6.3%), 3,780 in 2025. The dossier attributes rising prices to regen-culture demand, to migration of people moving for climate reasons and to California capital (not verified).
source: USDA NASS Land Values 2024 Summary (opened, Oregon statewide); Farmer Mac 2024 U.S. Farmland Values Report (not opened)
gaps: No Willamette Valley or Western Oregon price from an opened source; the band is therefore not computed.

price_notes: USDA NASS Land Values 2024 Summary, Vermont farm real estate 4,350 USD/acre (about 10,749 USD/ha; +5.1% on 2023; 4,400 in 2025). The dossier's forested or recreational rural land (500 to 2,000 USD/acre) and buildable rural land with utilities (5,000 to 20,000 USD/acre) were not verified (not verified) and are not used for the range. Per-acre to per-ha via /0.4047.
source: USDA NASS Land Values 2024 Summary, Vermont
gaps: Statewide farm real estate; forest, recreational and buildable-lot prices were not found in an opened source.

price_notes: USDA NASS Land Values 2024 Summary, North Carolina farm real estate 5,190 USD/acre (about 12,825 USD/ha; +7.0%); the dossier's '5,150 USD/acre' and '+8.4% YoY' do not match the table. Western North Carolina unimproved rural farmland or forest 5,000 to 15,000 USD/acre (12,350 to 37,060 USD/ha), parcels with road access, views or Asheville proximity 15,000 to 30,000 USD/acre (37,000 to 74,100 USD/ha) and Buncombe County parcels above 50,000 USD/acre come from commentary and listing analyses that were not opened (not verified); the statewide NASS figure understates mountain land. Per-acre to per-ha via /0.4047.
appreciation_notes: NASS North Carolina farm real estate 4,850 (2023) to 5,190 USD/acre (2024), +7.0%; 5,470 in 2025. Mountain-land appreciation was not verified.
source: USDA NASS Land Values 2024 Summary, North Carolina (opened); unityknows.com 2025 analysis and Conserving Carolina commentary (not opened)
gaps: No Western North Carolina price from an opened source; the band is therefore not computed.

price_notes: USDA NASS Land Values 2024 Summary, Wisconsin: farm real estate 6,120 USD/acre (about 15,122 USD/ha) and cropland 6,800 USD/acre (about 16,801 USD/ha). Driftless mixed or wooded parcels at 3,500 to 6,500 USD/acre (8,600 to 16,000 USD/ha) depending on slope, road access and tillable share come from Farmland Intel and local listings that were not opened (not verified) and are not used for the range. Per-acre to per-ha via /0.4047.
appreciation_notes: NASS Wisconsin cropland 6,620 USD/acre (2023) to 6,800 (2024), +2.7%; 7,250 in 2025. The dossier's organic-premium effect around Viroqua, La Farge and Cashton was not verified.
source: USDA NASS Land Values 2024 Summary, Wisconsin; NASS Wisconsin Cash Rent and Land Values 2024
gaps: Statewide figures; no Driftless county price series was opened.

price_notes: USDA NASS Land Values 2024 Summary, Arkansas: pasture 3,270 USD/acre (about 8,080 USD/ha), farm real estate 4,110 USD/acre (about 10,157 USD/ha), cropland 3,600 (about 8,896 USD/ha). Recreational and timberland at 2,000 to 5,000 USD/acre and raw land in Sharp and Izard counties at 1,000 to 3,000 USD/acre come from vendor blogs (Shamrock Lands, Mossy Oak Properties) and were not re-derived (not verified); they are not used for the range. Per-acre to per-ha via /0.4047.
appreciation_notes: NASS Arkansas farm real estate 3,920 USD/acre (2023) to 4,110 (2024), +4.8%; 4,250 in 2025.
source: USDA NASS Land Values 2024 Summary, Arkansas
gaps: Statewide figures; no Ozark county price series from an opened source.

price_notes: Taos County median listing 12,846 USD/acre (about 31,740 USD/ha) and an average of about 23,529 USD/acre (about 58,137 USD/ha) on listed properties come from listing sites (LandSearch, LandBoss) that were not read (not verified). USDA NASS 2025: New Mexico statewide farm real estate 725 USD/acre (about 1,791 USD/ha), a statewide average dominated by range land. Per-acre to per-ha via /0.4047.
appreciation_notes: Dossier: regen-network visibility has attracted land speculators and short-term rental operators who inflate land values (not verified).
source: USDA NASS Land Values 2025 Summary, New Mexico (opened); LandSearch and LandBoss listing figures (not opened)
gaps: No systematic published price series for Taos dryland parcels; listing medians reflect an amenity premium. The band is therefore not computed.

price_notes: Statistics Canada table 32-10-0047-01, Nova Scotia farm land and buildings: 3,934 CAD/acre (2023), 4,075 (2024), 4,168 (2025); x2.471 = 9,720 to 10,299 CAD/ha. The earlier figures (3,913 and 4,120) were per-acre values stored in a per-hectare field. Cape Breton undeveloped rural land at 500 to 2,000 CAD/acre (about 1,236 to 4,942 CAD/ha) is a dossier statement (not verified).
appreciation_notes: Statistics Canada: 3,934 to 4,075 CAD/acre (+3.6% in 2024) and to 4,168 (+2.3% in 2025). FCC reports Nova Scotia +1.6% for 2025.
source: Statistics Canada table 32-10-0047-01 (farm land and buildings, July 1); FCC Farmland Values Report 2025
gaps: Provincial figures; Cape Breton transaction prices vary enormously by road access and water and were not found in an opened source.

price_notes: Kootenay ALR cultivated valley benches 15,000 to 45,000 CAD/acre (about 37,000 to 111,200 CAD/ha) and raw or Class 5 parcels 3,000 to 12,000 CAD/acre (about 7,410 to 29,650 CAD/ha) come from FCC and Young Agrarians listings that do not contain these figures at the cited pages (not verified); the 2018 mean of 45,073 CAD/acre was not found either. Verified context: Statistics Canada 32-10-0047-01 gives a British Columbia figure only, 10,181 CAD/acre in 2024 (about 25,160 CAD/ha) and 10,577 in 2025. 'Three to five times the Alentejo baseline' is a dossier statement (not verified). Per-acre to per-ha via /0.4047.
appreciation_notes: No Kootenay series was found. FCC reports British Columbia values up 5.0% in the first half of 2024 and down 1.7% in its 2025 report; the dossier's '21.1% decline in the Kootenay ALR sub-region' is not on the cited FCC page and is withdrawn.
source: Statistics Canada table 32-10-0047-01 (British Columbia, opened); FCC Farmland Values Report 2024 (opened, no Kootenay figure); Young Agrarians listings 2023 (not opened)
gaps: No Kootenay price from an opened source; the band is therefore not computed.

price_notes: Estrie and Eastern Townships 8,000 to 14,000 CAD/acre (about 20,000 to 35,000 CAD/ha) is a dossier estimate from regional comparables and FCC commentary, not a published series (not verified). The dossier's Québec provincial average of 17,720 CAD/acre is not what Statistics Canada table 32-10-0047-01 shows (Québec 11,131 CAD/acre in 2025, about 27,500 CAD/ha), so it is dropped. Per-acre to per-ha via /0.4047.
appreciation_notes: Statistics Canada: Québec 6,656 CAD/acre (2019) to 11,131 (2025), +67%; FCC reports Québec +4.8% for 2025. No Estrie series was found.
source: Statistics Canada table 32-10-0047-01 (Québec, opened); FCC Farmland Values Report (opened); Estrie range is a dossier estimate
gaps: The Estrie range is an estimate; no Estrie price from an opened source, so the band is not computed.

price_notes: Private-title rural parcels in highland Oaxaca roughly 3,000 to 15,000 USD/ha depending on access, improvements and proximity to Oaxaca City: practitioner real-estate guidance, indicative only and not verified. Most of Oaxaca's rural territory is ejido or communal land outside private-market pricing.
appreciation_notes: No appreciation figure was found.
source: Registro Agrario Nacional (pointer to the agrarian registry; no price series was opened); practitioner real-estate guidance 2024 (not opened)
gaps: No systematic published price series equivalent to European Eurostat data was found. Dossier explicitly states price confidence is LOW. No appreciation rate or YoY data. Majority of Oaxaca's rural territory is communal/ejido land outside private-market pricing entirely.

price_notes: County averages of agricultural land including buildings, USD per acre, 2022: Schuyler 3,972; Tompkins 3,994; Cayuga 4,355; Seneca 4,610; Yates 6,402; NY State 4,102. x2.471 = USD 9,815 (Schuyler) to 15,820 (Yates) per hectare. Range spans county averages, not individual sales. NY state farm real estate 2026: USD 4,500/acre (USD 11,120/ha), cropland 4,150, pasture 2,040 (NASS Land Values 2026 Summary, July 2026). Lakefront, wine-trail and Ithaca-fringe parcels are not priced separately (no source opened).
appreciation_notes: NY state farm real estate 3,720 (2022), 3,960 (2023), 4,150 (2024), 4,300 (2025), 4,500 (2026): +21 percent over four years, +4.7 percent 2025-26 (USDA NASS Land Values 2026 Summary, July 2026). State-level only.
source: USDA NASS Census of Agriculture 2022 (county); USDA NASS Land Values 2026 Summary (July 2026)
gaps: Lakefront, wine-trail and Ithaca-fringe prices; county-level 2025 values; forest and rough-land prices; Farm Credit East and county cash rents not retrievable.

price_notes: USDA NASS Land Values 2025 Summary, Virginia state averages: pasture 5,300 USD/acre (13,097 USD/ha), farm real estate 6,100 (15,073), cropland 6,170 (15,246); /0.4047 per hectare. State-wide, not the three counties: parcels near Lake Anna waterfront, Charlottesville or Richmond commuter roads are likely to sit above this range (no county or waterfront price was obtained).
appreciation_notes: Virginia farm real estate +4.3% 2024 to 2025 (5,850 to 6,100) and +32.6% since 2021 (4,600); cropland +4.0%, pasture +4.1% in 2025. The 3 counties grew 10.8% in population in five years, an upward pressure not measured in prices here.
source: USDA NASS, Land Values 2025 Summary (August 2025), Virginia rows
gaps: No county-level or Lake Anna waterfront price; the statewide NASS figures are verified but the dossier says exurban and lake parcels likely sit above the state average, so the footprint's own prices are not known and the band is not computed. 2026 NASS summary not reached.

price_notes: No official, current Bas-Saint-Laurent price per hectare was found. The only regional figure (La Financière agricole du Québec, quoted by Radio-Canada, 16 December 2019: 6,000-6,500 CAD per hectare versus 20,000-22,000 provincially) is stale and is not shipped as a price. Province-wide context, Statistics Canada table 32-10-0047-01 (farm land and buildings, July 1): Québec 6,656 CAD per acre in 2019 and 11,131 in 2025.
appreciation_notes: Provincial: +67% from 2019 to 2025 (6,656 to 11,131 CAD per acre, Statistics Canada 32-10-0047-01) and +4.6% from 2024 to 2025; FCC reports Québec +4.8% for 2025. Radio-Canada (2019) reported regional prices had doubled in five years. No regional series after 2019 was found.
source: Statistics Canada 32-10-0047-01; FCC Farmland Values Report (2025 page); Radio-Canada 16 Dec 2019 citing La Financière agricole du Québec
gaps: Regional per-hectare price unavailable; FCC publishes provincial figures only; La Financière agricole regional series not located.

price_notes: Low end: Missouri average pasture value 2,850 USD/acre in 2026 (USDA NASS, July 2026), /0.404686 = 7,040 USD/ha. High end: Lee County, Iowa average farmland 10,222 USD/acre on 1 Nov 2025 (ISU Land Value Survey county estimate), = 25,260 USD/ha. Other anchors: Iowa farm real estate 10,100 USD/acre and Missouri 5,200 USD/acre (NASS 2026); Iowa counties 1 Nov 2025: Appanoose 6,679, Davis 7,735, Van Buren 8,438 USD/acre. No county-level Missouri values were found for Schuyler, Scotland or Clark. Documents: NASS Land Values 2026 Summary https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/sites/default/release-files/795999/land0726.pdf (Missouri pasture 2,850; farm real estate 5,200; Iowa 10,100); ISU county map as source_url. The two ends are different land classes (Missouri pasture, Iowa all-farmland average), so the band is a bracket, not a like-for-like range.
appreciation_notes: NASS 2026 farm real estate: Iowa +3.2 percent, Missouri +4.0 percent (state, 2025 to 2026). ISU 1 Nov 2025 county estimates fell slightly from 2024 in all four footprint counties (Appanoose 6,840 to 6,679; Davis 7,761 to 7,735; Van Buren 8,471 to 8,438; Lee 10,271 to 10,222); Iowa statewide +0.7 percent.
source: USDA NASS Land Values 2026 Summary (31 Jul 2026); Iowa State University Land Value Survey 2025 (county estimates, released 9 Dec 2025)
gaps: No Missouri county-level price series for the three Missouri counties; the low end is a statewide pasture benchmark, not a county figure; cash rents not retrieved.

price_notes: Low: Washington County average market value of land and buildings per farm acre, 2,136 USD/acre in the 2022 Census of Agriculture (Table 8), x 2.47105 = 5,278 USD/ha. High: Maine average cropland value 2026, 4,700 USD/acre (NASS Land Values 2026 Summary, July 2026), x 2.47105 = 11,614 USD/ha; Maine all farm real estate 3,400 USD/acre = 8,401 USD/ha and pasture 2,700 USD/acre = 6,672 USD/ha. Mixed county 2022 and state 2026 sources; farm-sector averages (blueberry barrens, woodland and buildings), not forest or shorefront sale prices, which were not found.
appreciation_notes: Nominal: Washington County farm land and buildings 1,534 to 2,136 USD/acre, +39% 2017 to 2022 (Census of Agriculture Table 8); Maine farm real estate 3,090 to 3,400 USD/acre, +10% 2022 to 2026 (NASS), against +21% for the US (3,720 to 4,500). Separate from farmland: the county's economic council estimates that 59% of households cannot afford to buy a home (June 2026). Out-of-state buyer pressure could not be sourced and is not claimed.
source: USDA NASS Census of Agriculture 2022 (Washington County, Table 8); USDA NASS Land Values 2026 Summary (July 2026); Sunrise County Economic Council housing page
gaps: No county farmland value after 2022; no forest, shorefront or timberland sale prices; no county house-price series (MaineHousing dashboards are interactive and could not be read); band is a qualitative gloss on farm-sector averages, not a market recommendation.
